articles.title: Pakistan Refuses to Repatriate Rochdale Grooming Gang Leader
articles.excerpt: During a meeting with UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband, Pakistan's Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar stated that there is no mechanism for extraditing Shabir Ahmed, a key figure in the Rochdale grooming gang.
articles.content_html:
BREAKING NEWS — LIVE

Live updates, newest first.

15:27, 28 August 2026

During a meeting with UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband, Pakistan's Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar stated that there is no mechanism for extraditing Shabir Ahmed, a key figure in the Rochdale grooming gang.

Pakistan has declined the United Kingdom's request to extradite Shabir Ahmed, a ringleader of the Rochdale grooming gang, during a meeting between UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband and Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar.

Ishaq Dar stated that there is 'no bilateral mechanism' in place to facilitate the return of Ahmed, who has been convicted of child sexual exploitation in the UK.

The refusal comes amid ongoing discussions about the UK government's efforts to address issues related to child exploitation and the management of offenders abroad.

This development may have implications for local authorities in Rochdale as they continue to deal with the aftermath of the grooming scandal.

articles.title: Restoration of Historic Packer Spout Steps Completed in Rochdale Town Centre
articles.excerpt: The restoration of the Packer Spout steps, a historic landmark in Rochdale, has been completed, linking key attractions and preserving local heritage.
articles.content_html:
The restoration of the Packer Spout steps, a historic feature in Rochdale town centre, has been successfully completed. These steps, which date back to before 1660, connect the Rochdale Town Hall area with St Chad’s Church, the oldest church in the borough, which has parts dating back to Saxon times.

The steps, located within the Broadfield Park Slopes, have a rich history, believed to have been used by mourning relatives who would ascend to St Chad’s Church to scatter rue and rosemary in the churchyard. The area surrounding the steps was notorious during the Victorian era for its high crime rates and poor living conditions, known as 'the gank'.

Contractors Maysand faced significant challenges during the restoration due to the steepness of the site, necessitating a special pulley system to transport materials. The project involved the careful removal of all 122 steps, many of which were damaged, and their reconstruction using traditional sandstone to maintain historical accuracy. Recycled materials were also incorporated into the restoration, along with the addition of a new handrail.

Councillor Danny Meredith, cabinet member for regeneration at Rochdale Borough Council, expressed his satisfaction with the project, stating that the restored steps are a vital part of Rochdale's heritage and enhance the town centre's conservation area. The completion of this project complements the recent restoration of Rochdale Town Hall and Broadfield Park, contributing to the overall aesthetic and historical significance of the area.

articles.title: Lift Out of Service at Derker Tram Stop
articles.excerpt: The lift at Derker tram stop is currently out of service, affecting access for passengers. Alternative step-free access routes are available for travel towards and away from Manchester.
articles.content_html:
The lift at Derker tram stop is out of service as of 7:32pm on Thursday, 27 August 2026, and will remain unavailable until further notice. This disruption affects passengers using the tram stop for travel towards Manchester and Rochdale.

For customers travelling towards Manchester, step-free access is available via a ramp from Cromford Street directly to the Manchester-bound platform. Passengers heading away from Manchester can also use a ramp from Cromford Street, followed by a track crossing to reach the Rochdale-bound platform.

Transport for Greater Manchester has issued an apology for any inconvenience caused by this service disruption. Passengers are advised to plan their journeys accordingly and consider alternative routes if necessary.

Further updates regarding the lift's status will be provided as they become available. For more information, visit the Transport for Greater Manchester website.
